problem: Object navigation agents have only a first-person, limited-visibility view, which makes global planning hard. Prior ego-centric visual representations do not capture object relationships or long-term history efficiently.
motivation: Agents must find target objects in unfamiliar indoor scenes from partial observations. An informative, efficient ego-centric representation that models both local and global object-scene relations, and that aggregates memory across time steps, should support better target association and longer-horizon search.
key_idea: Build a temporal scene-object graph that combines a holistic object feature descriptor, a scene-object graph capturing local and global correlations, and a temporal graph aggregation module over past steps.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that describing objects from several aspects (HOFD) helps relate observed and unseen objects. It also claims that joint local and global graph learning (SOG) helps target association, and that temporal aggregation (TGA) helps in longer trajectories.
method: Holistic Object Feature Descriptor (HOFD): describes each object from several aspects to support learning relations between observed and unseen objects.
Scene-Object Graph (SOG): learns local and global correlations between objects and the agent's observations for scene understanding and target association.
Temporal Graph Aggregation (TGA): dynamically aggregates memory information across consecutive time steps to give a dynamic view of history for longer trajectories.
